game: Week 7 GB@DET / kickoff not in pack / DET -4 / total 55.5 / weather not saved

script.base: Market prices a high-scoring DET lean: implied about DET 29.75 / GB 25.75. Base flow is competitive into the 4th with Detroit up by a score, both QBs throwing. Goff is the better blitz QB (EPA +0.41 on 68 blitz dropbacks vs +0.22 clean) into GB's 34% blitz, so DET stays pass-inclusive even with a lead; Gibbs still gets a heavy carry share (60 carries, 296 yards over the last 3) because DET is the favorite. Love mostly sees DET's 30% blitz rate, so more of his dropbacks are the no-blitz look where his EPA is +0.20, not the -0.02 blitz look.
script.flip1: GB scores first and leads at half. DET abandons early run balance, Gibbs' rush line dies, and targets pile onto LaPorta, St. Brown, Williams and TeSlaa. That helps LaPorta over and can push St. Brown toward 84.5, which is why that unpriced under was not a leg.
script.flip2: DET jumps up 14+ early and grinds clock with Gibbs (20 carries/game recently). GB pass volume stalls until garbage, Golden's deep shots (401 air yards over 3 games) die, and LaPorta becomes target-dependent rather than script-proof.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice trend, or inactives in the pack, so fallout is inferred only from who actually touched the ball. DET L3 usage is intact: Gibbs 60/296 rush and 21 targets, St. Brown 30 targets, LaPorta 22, Williams 16, TeSlaa 13, Vaki 12 carries, Wright 5 targets, Goff 3 rushes. GB L3 rushers are a committee with no Josh Jacobs: Lloyd 25/54, K. Johnson 16/66, Strong 16/35, Brooks 4/30. Jacobs props exist with team tag nan and zero L3 carries in this pack, so his 47.5 rush / 61.5 rush+rec lines are a pass, not an edge. Lloyd (18 rush yds/game, 2.16 YPC) and Strong (11.7 rush, 16.7 rec) only clear short lines if that committee holds; a Jacobs return not in the pack kills both. Final inactives unknown.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone charting not in pack. Location splits only: DET middle is the hole; GB has no location hole.
matchup.pressure: DET blitzes 30%. Love EPA/dropback -0.02 vs blitz (n=91) vs +0.20 with no blitz, so most GB dropbacks are the good look, but any pressure that gets home (pressure rate not in pack) kills Golden's 14.3 air yards/target. GB blitzes 34%. Goff EPA +0.41 vs blitz (n=68) vs +0.22 clean, so GB's blitz is a DET offensive edge, not a sack script.
matchup.bleeds: DET: middle 10.98 YPA on 43 att vs left 5.78 (72 att) and right 7.49 (96 att); 23 passes of 20+ on 234 att; rush YPC allowed 4.48 and 17 runs of 10+ in 5 games. GB: left 6.56 (72), middle 6.09 (47), right 5.46 (91); only 9 passes of 20+ on 228 att; rush YPC allowed 4.14 and 14 runs of 10+ in 6 games.
matchup.overlap: Priced overlap that survives the line: Golden's deep target lead (28 targets, 401 air yards) into DET's explosive leak (23 of 20+), with DET blitzing only 30%. Kraft is the true middle overlap (20 targets, 61 air yards) into DET's 10.98 middle YPA, but he averaged 47.7 rec yards vs a 51.5 line, so that lean was dropped. LaPorta is not attacking a GB bleed — GB middle is only 6.09 YPA — but he is the intermediate piece of an offense that gets better when GB blitzes, and 49.5 sits 22 yards under his L3 role.

form: Avoiding season averages. GB L3 receiving: Golden 28 tgt / 248 yds / 401 air (82.7 yds/game); Watson 19/254/347 (84.7, line 77 but price +nan); Kraft 20/143/61 (47.7 vs 51.5). GB rush committee inefficient: Lloyd 2.16 YPC, Strong 2.19 YPC. DET L3: Gibbs 98.7 rush yds/game and 47.7 rec (rush+rec 146.3 vs 139.5 line, thin); LaPorta 22 tgt / 216 yds / 202 air (72.0 vs 49.5); Williams 16/198/302 (66.0 vs 54.5) but that is bomb production GB has not allowed (9 explosives in 6 games), so the over was not the read and the under was dropped because form disagrees; St. Brown 30/163/247 (54.3 vs 84.5) with air yards fighting an under; TeSlaa 13/161/159 (53.7 vs 24.5) looks spike-prone without game logs and needs explosives GB suppresses. Passed: Jacobs (no L3 role), Kraft over (form under the line), Williams either side, TeSlaa, Gibbs 95.5/139.5 (cushion under 7 yards vs a 4.14 YPC GB run defense).

edge_players.edge_sentence: LaPorta has been a real downfield weapon, not a checkdown, at 72 receiving yards a game on 7.3 targets and 202 air yards, and 49.5 asks him to fall 22 yards under that role in a 55.5 game where Goff's EPA jumps to +0.41 against the blitz GB uses 34% of the time.
edge_players.must_be_true: LaPorta plays his normal snap share, DET stays pass-inclusive even if they lead by a score, and he holds about 6+ targets rather than ceding the intermediate to St. Brown or Gibbs.
edge_players.kills_it: DET leads by 14+ and grinds Gibbs (20 carries/game in the L3), or GB takes the intermediate away and the 22 targets/3 games consolidate onto Williams' bombs. Inactives are not in the pack, so a late LaPorta scratch kills it outright.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Golden is GB's target leader at 9.3 per game and 83 receiving yards, with 401 air yards, and Detroit has allowed 23 gains of 20+ yards while blitzing only 30%, so Love mostly gets the no-blitz dropbacks where his EPA is +0.20.
edge_players.must_be_true: Golden keeps the WR1 target share, GB is trailing or in a shootout so the pass volume stays up, and at least one deep shot connects the way 248 yards on 401 air already has.
edge_players.kills_it: Uncharted pressure speeds Love up, Watson (254 yards on only 19 targets) steals the explosives, or GB leads early and the Lloyd/Johnson/Strong committee closes it out. DET's real bleed is the middle (10.98 YPA), not the outside, so a shadow on Golden with no middle involvement loses the leg.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot price a true edge or test the 70% calibration warning. Available form agrees with both kept legs: LaPorta 72.0 vs 49.5 and Golden 82.7 vs 73.5. Dropped leans where the pack disagreed: Kraft over (47.7 vs 51.5), Williams under (66.0 vs 54.5), TeSlaa under (53.7 vs 24.5). St. Brown under 84.5 was not kept because 247 air yards on 30 targets is opportunity data fighting a lean under, and the price is +nan. No model probability above 70% is being claimed.

market_rung_price: samlaporta recyds over 49.5 -113.5; matthewgolden recyds over 73.5 -114. No alt rungs in the pack. Do not add short-priced alts. St. Brown 84.5 and Watson 77 are +nan and were not used.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because GB's pass defense (9 gains of 20+ on 228 attempts, no location above 6.56 YPA) took LaPorta's intermediate away and he finished near 35-40 while Goff's blitz EPA showed up in Williams or St. Brown instead. Golden lost because 401 air yards already mean a pile of incomplete deep shots, DET's weakness is the middle not the outside a 14.3 air-yards-per-target receiver lives on, Watson took the one explosive, and pressure on non-blitz dropbacks — rate not in the pack — sped Love up. A Jacobs return absent from the L3 rush log would also have cut GB pass volume if the game stayed inside the -4.
slip_story: One shootout story at 55.5 with DET -4: GB trails and throws (Golden over) while DET stays pass-inclusive and Goff attacks GB's 34% blitz (LaPorta over). These two win together. Do not pair them with a game under, with Gibbs rush-only in a blowout script, or with St. Brown/Williams overs that need the same DET targets LaPorta is living on.
